82108.subject: Weekly Recap: Binance Reopens as Its Hackers Keep Moving Funds
82108.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

**Binance** spent the week reopening withdrawals and explaining how attackers took $6.34 billion, while the attackers kept converting what Binance could not freeze. **Democrats** won both chambers of Congress, and by our count the CLARITY Act is still 11 votes short of ending debate in the Senate.

Security incidents kept landing on infrastructure. A Linux kernel flaw kept **Threshold**'s tBTC bridge offline all week, a **reth** client bug led vaults and bridges to pause, and **Gnosis Pay** confirmed a breach that exposed card customers' home addresses and wallet addresses. **Polygon** validators were asked to approve a hard fork that would hand stolen POL back to its owners.

Enjoy!

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### WATCH

## THORChain Refused to Block the $387M Bitget Hacker. Here’s Why | Chad Barraford

Youtube: THORChain Refused to Block the $387M Bitget Hacker. Here’s Why | Chad Barraford (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h5i3zElaKxc)

**Chad Barraford**, THORChain's technical co-founder, explains why THORChain did not block the hacker behind Bitget's $387 million theft. The FBI has since asked THORChain node operators to block funds from the Binance hack, and this week the attackers swapped XRP into bitcoin through THORChain. [**Listen to the episode.**](https://thedefiant.io/news/podcast/thorchain-refused-to-block-the-usd387m-bitget-hacker-here-s-why-or-chad-barraford)

———————————————————————————

# Top Stories This Week

## Binance Reopens Withdrawals and Traces Its Hack to a Fake Job Interview

Binance [began reopening withdrawals](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-begins-reopening-withdrawals-with-bitcoin-after-6-3-billion-hack) on Sunday, starting with bitcoin, and its tracked wallets [posted a $4.54 billion net outflow](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-posts-4-54-billion-net-outflow-as-tracked-rivals-gain-564-million) in the first hours. On Tuesday, a [technical report](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-details-months-long-campaign-behind-6-34-billion-hack) traced the theft to a fake job interview in September. Malware from a coding assignment let the attackers reach Binance's wallet-signing service, which signed an EIP-7702 delegation that let an outside contract empty a hot wallet. By our arithmetic, Binance cleared that delegation 3 hours and 46 minutes after the first sweep. It put the funds frozen or intercepted at about $2.85 billion, and its wallets [swung back to net inflows](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/binance-flips-to-1-82-billion-in-daily-net-inflows-after-withdrawal-restart). On Wednesday, Binance [widened its proof of reserves to 44 tokens](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-expands-proof-of-reserves-to-44-tokens-after-hack) and said it had replaced about 98% of the stolen assets, and THORChain [restarted most swaps](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/thorchain-restarts-most-swaps-with-14-nodes-yet-to-upgrade). 🧠 Crypto News Brief: Extreme fear grips crypto as Bitcoin sinks to an 11-week low and ETF redemptions mount. Washington pulls both ways: Treasury cuts off MEXC and drops a surveillance rule, while a crypto-in-401(k) rule reaches the White House. 🚫 US Treasury Cuts MEXC Off From the US Financial System FinCEN has designated MEXC Global a primary money laundering concern and ordered US financial institutions to stop processing any transfers to or from the exchange. Treasury alleges the top-20 platform handled at least $16 billion in illicit flows between May 2021 and May 2026, tied to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and networks linked to Iran and North Korea. The order takes effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. Read full story 📉 Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $412M as BTC Sinks to 11-Week Low US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $412 million on November 6, a second straight day of heavy redemptions, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for about $403 million while Fidelity's FBTC was the lone fund with inflows. Ether ETFs shed another $93 million, and year-to-date Bitcoin ETF flows have now slipped into negative territory as BTC hovers near $75,000–$76,000 after an AI-stock selloff. More details 🏦 Crypto in 401(k) Plans Moves Closer as Rule Reaches White House The US Department of Labor has sent a proposed rule to the White House's regulatory review office that would open 401(k) retirement plans to alternative assets, including crypto, following President Trump's executive order. The rule would set criteria for fiduciaries weighing higher costs against diversification and long-term returns, a push Senators Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders have opposed. Read more 🏛️ Treasury Withdraws $250 Crypto Travel Rule Proposal FinCEN and the Federal Reserve have rescinded a 2020 proposal that would have cut the travel-rule reporting threshold for transfers from $3,000 to $250, citing its age and how much the crypto industry has changed. Coin Center and the Crypto Council for Innovation welcomed the move, which follows October's withdrawal of proposed rules on self-hosted wallets and crypto mixing. 82102.body:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** It’s recap day, with this week’s five biggest stories and five tools to try this weekend. Claude started turning down requests to copy existing games, and OpenAI revealed the hidden model behind its recent hacks. ChatGPT learned to talk about your money, and days later Claude asked for a look at your bank account too. And Codex pushed so much code that OpenAI had to rebuild Git to keep up.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Games:** What kind of game will Claude refuse to build?

* **OpenAI:** Which model was behind OpenAI’s hacks?

* **ChatGPT:** Can you ask ChatGPT out loud where your paycheck went?

* **Claude:** Why does Claude want to see your bank account?

* **Git:** Why did OpenAI have to rebuild Git?


----------







----------
## Claude stopped building copycat games

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1fb8e6e3-1891-4dfb-be35-e8d8576820ab/a34970ce-fbda-4190-b1f7-0eee0bd7abe2.jpg?t=1793607591)
Caption: 

Claude Code now [turns you down](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/programming/anthropic-appears-to-have-ordered-ai-tool-claude-to-stop-remaking-video-games) if you ask it to build a game that sounds too much like one that already exists. Anthropic confirmed the change, saying that copying someone else’s game breaks its usage rules.

In recent weeks, several indie studios had pulled their public demos, worried that someone would hand them to an AI and release a copy first.

The rule caught more than copycats. One studio that makes digital board-wargame modules for paying customers says Claude started refusing its work right after it asked whether the new rule covered it.

Then Anthropic [softened the rule](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-loosens-game-restrictions-claude-will-now-offer-to-build-original-game-in-same-genre-if-asked-to-copy), and Claude now offers to build an original game in the same genre instead.


----------







----------
## OpenAI unveiled the model behind its hacks

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/277ded7a-f336-4716-be4b-d4f0e70a74a2/Nov_6_-_1.jpg?t=1793955489)
Caption: 

OpenAI released [GPT-6 Cyber](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber/), a model built to find and confirm security holes that attackers could use. It’s the first OpenAI model to earn a “Critical” cybersecurity rating, so only ve
